claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a steep learning curve and requires several hours to understand the core mechanics and controls.

citations.review_text: As a big fan of in depth survival games, this one takes it all for me. Don't let the graphics fool you as there is a lot more going on under the hood than meets the eye. I will admit that for how complex it is, really took a few hours for it to all sink in and finally click. Having an absolute blast now!
Really great game, pretty hefty learning curve but once you get a hang of it you can spend hours enjoying it, really fun to play with friends as well.

This is my first endeavor into this survivalist genre. Once you understand how it plays it gets to be more fun. So yes, there is a learning curve. It's challenging enough to make me want to try again but not to much to where it's pointless to progress. I think it has great potential for more. The menus and searching functions are my only negative feedback. Equipping stuff is a little funky as well.

Very fun but difficult to understand the mechanics as a newbie, even with the guide. It's best to start off with a custom sandbox to lower the zombie population, just so you can get the hang of the mechanics.
really good. better with friends. thing is tho you have to spend a lot of time getting to understand it. well atleast i needed atleast 10 hrs to understand what im doing somewhat.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Sandbox survival provides open-ended freedom despite poorly explained mechanics and sloppy combat targeting.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks an official in-game story, focusing instead on sandbox survival.

citations.review_text:
It's a good game to play if you like survival and crafting. It has a lot of stuff to do, and a lot of realistic mechanics like learning to cook, crafting, and there's a ton of tools to work with. But the main thing is there's no story inside the game apart from surviving — in a future update it could have a story, but for now the main objective is just to survive as long as you can, that's it.

Plays good solo or with friends, works both ways.

My personal rating: 6.5/10

genually best game out there when it comes to zombie survival, it lacks a few features like vehicle modifications, but there are plenty of mods for that, even though vanilla would be better. same thing goes for lore, there is no real start or ending, you just sort of spawn in and play. i cant blame that on the devs though, they are totally putting a lot of work in and it takes time, its still one of the best games ever, though it totally needs a little more work and polishing, but its already good as it is, i mean even when playing on a test unstable version i got zero bugs, and even though im on a pretty old laptop it runs suprisingly well. certainly recommended.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe a steep learning curve and mechanics that are difficult to grasp or poorly explained initially.

citations.review_text: This game is beautiful. It feels like it's super hard to learn and understand, until you start to learn and understand it. There's still plenty that needs to be implemented but it's easily playable in it's current state. Plenty of content and lots of zombies. <3

Started playing once build 42 went stable. Having a lot of fun with this and the depth of the mechanics is awesome. bit of a learning curve but not too bad.

There are some frustration and rough edges however. Some of the mechanics are not explained well i.e. training skills and the requirements. Inventory management is a chore and the interface is not well fantastic.

Otherwise an interesting experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the isometric targeting system can fail or feel sloppy during combat, leading to missed melee attacks.

citations.review_text: Not sure when the last time I played was before coming back to try build 42. Had to at least be a few years. The game seems much bigger with better loot and better environment. But i spend hours starting a new character, looting and fighting until the targeting system would inevitably fail to target the only zombie in front of me even though the cursor is right over him and Id get bit and have to start over. I mean literally, the zombie would be highlighted and all of a sudden as he gets within range it un selects, he closes in as my swing misses but clips through his body in the animation, and now ive wasted a few hours. Had this happen so many times back to back to back in the short hours I'm just going to uninstall again. I remember the game being hard but the melee always worked fine. Put mouse in general direction, swing, character hits zombie. For an isometric game it worked. Maybe it was still targeting but somethings off about it now. That plus a bunch of other bugs, stuttering when zooming in or out or walking between cells, destroying vehicles and coming to a complete stop on what shouldn't even be a hiccup for them... IDK 13 years and counting and what's here isn't grabbing me any more than it did years ago, and now, the melee which is most of a zombie survival game, isn't working half the time causing me to waste my own time which I dont have enough of. Pass on this game unless youre ok with the possibility of losing a ton of progress to something out of your control.

I'm really torn but I don't think I can recommend this. There are plenty of other games in the genre that are much better, like 7 Days. The isometric targeting is what kills it for me. It's very sloppy and you click in the wrong place (which has a very wide range) and you die. If the targeting was tightened up I'd probably push through, but it's just a dumb grind at this point.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight unforgiving gameplay alongside connection errors and multiplayer performance issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe experiencing lag, performance drops, and crashes when playing multiplayer or driving through towns on the stable build.

citations.review_text:
I have played almost 900 hours of this game. It has, in recent months, become my favorite game of all time. But with the release of B42 "stable" (honestly, if you can even call it stable), the game is unplayable. Visually, it has been beautiful! I'm very pleased with most of the new additions and remakes. But everything I am happy with gets outweighed by everything bad. 

You can play B42 for about an hour minimum before the lag becomes unplayable. Driving through towns specifically is hell. Even regular co-op *WITH MODS* is hard to run, borderline unplayable as well. They have successfully made a stable version for single-player, while screwing up multiplayer. While in the rest stop in Muldraugh (I was playing in mp for this, surprisingly), one of us had an issue where a van was spawning on the roof on their end, and on my end two vans were spawned inside the kitchen.

Reverting to B41 doesn't fix anything, because even then you're unable to host servers, again, even without mods. I am honestly, to put it in nicer words, flabbergasted at this release. How did anybody on the team think this was a good idea to release this this way? You even had *streamers* play hours before officially releasing this, and nobody thought to say anything? Playing on B41 with 300+ mods is easier to run than B42 *STABLE* without mods.

I have honestly lost all my respect and admiration for this game.
I do not come from a wealthy background, and i am not old enough to generate my own income. With that being said, my laptop is not exactly ideal for running this game. However it does have the minimum requirements for the game ( that is listed under the store page ).
With the new B42 update i cant even boot up the game anymore before it crashes on me. I have tried absolutely everything to get it going. Nothing works. I understand that this game is early access, but the game has been early access for 12 years. It is absolutely insane that a game has been in early access so long and cannot support the minimum requirements it needs to run.
On top of this i had to wait almost 2 years for the game to release B42 in stable. Why are the updates so far out from each other? After all this time waiting I cannot even run it on my laptop that is supposed to be able to run it.

This isn't even my last issue with the game. Multiplayer is so extremely difficult for me, i have a good Wi-Fi speed and i still lag extremely when playing with friends, and when i try to make a server it is unplayable for others in the sense that chunks of the map don't load and zombies appear and disappear out of thin air. This is why i almost exclusively play solo but now i cant even open the game.
It sucks to already play on everything set to the minimum graphics to even remotely be able to play the game. The screen is super small, everything is choppy and looks like cardboard.

I was honestly so excited for the development of this game, but now i get spat in the face because i cannot afford a good computer.
Stable my ass. Love the game btw but the game crashed on me and my friends at the military base 13 times im angry rn.

claims.claim: Reviewers report connection errors, loading difficulties, and trouble hosting or joining servers in multiplayer.

citations.review_text:
If you want to play the sandbox solo, go ahead and buy it, install some mods, and enjoy.

Want to have more fun and play online with other people? Forget it.

The pace of development and updates is simply terrible.

For example, the game still has a multiplayer login bug that can make it physically impossible to connect or reconnect to a server. Sometimes various ridiculous workarounds help, but the issue itself has never gone away.

Support has been notified about it multiple times. With every ticket, they asked for additional information and suggested the most basic troubleshooting steps, none of which actually helped and only wasted your time. Eventually, they acknowledged that it was a bug and said it had been given high priority.

More than a week has passed, and there is still no fix, even though two hotfix updates have been released in the meantime.

And this is despite the fact that one kind soul provided a thorough, detailed report with debug logs and even pointed out exactly where the client-side issue was.

What is the point of buying a broken product and then wasting your own time trying to fix it?

This game is super frustrating, instead of having a single streamlined multiplayer system, it has a very frustrating and confusing multiplayer system where it is nearly impossible to join any server, except for vanilla servers, which are like 1-2 servers with like 10-15 players mostly, and the few servers that have population are heavily modded, which this game keeps giving me connection errors, just plain errors, and cant connect messages while i spent a long time downloading all the ♥♥♥♥ for each server.... this is just frustrating the multiplayer is ass.

game pretty much sucks without mods, game is desolate and boring on singleplayer, game does not run or synchronize for ♥♥♥♥ on multiplayer (even worse with mods) unless you use a dedicated server which isn't even guaranteed to do anything

claims.claim: Reviewers mention a steep learning curve and a challenging, unforgiving experience for new players.

citations.review_text: Love this game - very steep learning curve but if you like survival games, this is it.

It's like "Sims 4" but if it was good. And there's Zombies.... a lot of Zombies.

This game has a steep difficulty curve that might frustrate you, but trust me, if you stick with it, it will be more than worth it.

Overall the best realistic zombie apocalypse game out there. Has a steep learning curve but it feels so rearding. The game gets updated very regularly and overall has an incredible dev team behind it. If you want to play a truky realistic zombie game, buy it
